note: Curated drug-target complexes selected from experimentally determined structures. Ligand codes and protein titles were read from the deposited PDB files and the RCSB entry API, not from memory. Interaction values are computed at request time from the deposited coordinates. Catalytic-residue identities are literature facts and are labelled as such; the statement that a given residue is (or is not) in contact is measured.

complexes.protein_title: Crystal structure at 1.9 A resolution of HIV II protease complexed with L-735,524 (indinavir)
complexes.mechanism_summary: HIV-1 protease is a homodimeric aspartic protease that cleaves the viral Gag-Pol polyprotein into the mature structural and enzymatic proteins the virus needs to become infectious. Indinavir is a peptidomimetic inhibitor shaped like the substrate transition state, so it binds the same active site the polyprotein would occupy.
complexes.consequence: Because the polyprotein is never cleaved, the virus assembles non-infectious, immature virions. This is why HIV protease inhibitors must be present continuously: they block a step of maturation, not the production of viral RNA.
sources: PDB entry 1HSG - Chen et al., J. Biol. Chem. 1994, 'Crystal structure at 1.9 A resolution of HIV II protease complexed with L-735,524'

complexes.protein_title: High resolution structures of HIV-1 RT from four RT-inhibitor complexes
complexes.target_class: Viral RNA-dependent DNA polymerase (HIV-1 reverse transcriptase)
complexes.mechanism_summary: Reverse transcriptase copies the viral RNA genome into DNA, which the virus then inserts into the host chromosome. Nevirapine is a non-nucleoside inhibitor: it does not look like a nucleotide and does not bind the polymerase active site. It occupies a hydrophobic allosteric pocket in the p66 subunit roughly 10 A from the catalytic residues and locks the enzyme in an inactive conformation.
complexes.consequence: With the enzyme held in that inactive shape, viral RNA is never copied into DNA and the replication cycle stops before integration. Because the site is allosteric rather than catalytic, a single point mutation in the pocket (for example K103N or Y181C) is often enough to abolish binding, which is why NNRTI resistance emerges readily.

complexes.display_name: Influenza A neuraminidase with Oseltamivir carboxylate
complexes.protein_title: N1 neuraminidase in complex with oseltamivir
complexes.target_class: Viral sialidase (influenza A neuraminidase, N1 subtype)
complexes.mechanism_summary: Neuraminidase is the influenza enzyme that clips sialic acid residues off the surface of the infected cell and off newly budded virions. That clipping is what releases progeny virions so they can spread. Oseltamivir carboxylate is a transition-state analogue: its cyclohexene scaffold and carboxylate present the same features the enzyme recognises in its sialic-acid substrate, so it binds the catalytic site.
complexes.consequence: New virions stay tethered to the infected cell and clump together instead of spreading, so the infection does not amplify efficiently. The enzyme is blocked, not the virus's entry or its genome copying.
sources: PDB entry 2HU4 - Russell et al., Nature 2006, 'The structure of H5N1 avian influenza neuraminidase suggests new opportunities for drug design'

complexes.display_name: Human angiotensin-converting enzyme with Lisinopril (human enzyme example, not a virus)
complexes.protein_title: Crystal structure of human angiotensin converting enzyme in complex with lisinopril
complexes.mechanism_summary: Angiotensin-converting enzyme is a human zinc metallopeptidase that converts angiotensin I into the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II and degrades bradykinin. Lisinopril carries a carboxylate that coordinates the catalytic zinc ion and occupies the substrate-binding channel.
complexes.consequence: With the enzyme blocked, angiotensin II production falls and bradykinin is preserved, which lowers blood pressure. This is a human drug target, included as an example of the same method applied to a non-viral enzyme. The structure also contains a zinc ion, chloride ions and a glycated lysine, all of which are excluded from the ligand analysis because they are not the drug.
sources: PDB entry 1O86 - Natesh et al., Nature 2003, 'Crystal structure of the human angiotensin-converting enzyme-lisinopril complex'
